thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging alert: Canary cluster r5 reported p99 > 2.5s for the last 3m across streaming endpoints. Investigate and mitigate.

alex: saw it too. Canary rollout of model-redwood-v12 started ~5m ago and traffic was shifted to 10%. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~700ms, p99 to ~2.8s. Streaming stalls reported from a subset of pods.

maria: confirming. Traces show long encoder queue times and a spike in kv-cache misses on the canary shard. Link to traces: https://traces.internal/redwood/canary/3799999999

alex: posting quick logs snippet from one affected pod:

```
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] encoder_queue_length=34
[2026-03-15T14:12:04Z] kv_cache_hit=0.12 kv_cache_miss=0.88
[2026-03-15T14:12:05Z] token_stream_delay_ms=2200
```

alex: immediate ask: (1) pause canary traffic shift to v12 and route back to v11, (2) scale canary pool by +25% if rollback takes time, (3) keep tracing on. I'll start rollback if we agree.

tj: agree to rollback. I'll flip routing to v11 and monitor. Oncall runbook recommends rollback for tail latency regressions on canary.

li: quick note — the v12 build included a change to KV prefetch logic (PR #8833). If prefetch is causing thundering, rolling back should help.

nina: I'm on scaling now, triggering an immediate +2 instance autoscale on the canary ASG and bumping burst capacity. Giving ETA ~90s for new pods to be ready.

sam-support: flagged high-sev customer alerts to SRE leads and created a customer impact spreadsheet. No direct customer tickets yet, but latency-sensitive customers on streaming may see degraded UX.

alex: executing rollback now. Command:

```
redwood-cli routes promote --service=canary --from=model-redwood-v12 --to=model-redwood-v11 --percentage=100
```

alex: done. Routing change propagated across edge in ~25s.

incident-bot: change recorded: route-promote by alex at 3799999999.

maria: initial metrics post-rollback: p95 down to ~140ms within 90s, p99 trending to 320ms. Streaming in-flight stalls dropped. KV-cache miss rate is decreasing.

li: adding detail — the v12 kv-prefetch introduced a small race where concurrent prefetches cause high mem-copy contention on GPU host, which increases encoder queue time. We'll follow up with a patch to serialize prefetches and add a guard.

tj: good catch. For now, we should tag v12 as blocked for canary until fix. Setting rollout flag to 'halted' in the release dashboard.

nina: scaling reversed back to normal after rolling metrics stabilized. No ongoing autoscale.

sam-support: updating customers: posted to status page that a canary deployment caused transient latency increases and we've rolled back the model. No data loss or requests failed; only higher tail latency briefly.

alex: summary for the next oncall (handoff):
- Incident start: 3799999999 (alert from canary p99 > 2.5s)
- Root cause hypothesis: v12 kv-prefetch change causing mem contention -> encoder queueing -> streaming stalls and tail latency
- Actions taken: promoted route back to v11 (rollback), temporary autoscale during mitigation, tracing retained for postmortem, customers notified on status page
- Current status: Stable, p95/p99 back within SLOs, canary traffic stopped
- Followups: fix PR from li to serialize prefetch + e2e perf test for encoder queue under prefetch; re-run canary behind additional safety flags (limit concurrent prefetches to 2)

tj: handing off to next oncall @alex for evening. Please keep an eye on any regressions when we retest v12 with patch.

alex: taking handoff. I'll coordinate with li on the patch and schedule a slow canary replay with 1% traffic and metrics guardrails.

incident-bot: incident annotated: severity=high, impact=latency-spike, customer-impact=potential-streaming-degradation, status=mitigated, ticket=INC-2026-0423.

sam-support: adding a note to the customer impact spreadsheet: affected endpoints: /v1/stream, observed window: 14:10-14:15 UTC, potential affected customers: list attached.

maria: we'll run a targeted load test with v12+patch in staging and attach kv-cache hit/miss heatmaps to the postmortem.

li: assigning myself to the fix; will open PR within 2 hours.

alex: thanks everyone. If anything flares up I'll re-open paging. :thumbsup:
